title: Perimeter & Area Review, Arc Lengths & Sector Area: Angular Proportionality
description: Master the angular fraction principle connecting central angle θ to circumference and area. Rigorously derive Arc Length l = (θ/360) × 2πr and Sector Area A = (θ/360) × πr² = 1/2 × l × r. Understand minor sectors, major sectors, and quadrants.
key_concepts: Angular Fraction Principle: Since a full circle corresponds to 360°, a central angle of θ corresponds to the fractional part θ / 360°
Arc Length Formula: l = (θ / 360°) × 2πr
Area of Sector Formula: Area = (θ / 360°) × πr²
Kinetic Sector Relation: Area of sector = 1/2 × (Arc length) × Radius = 1/2 × l × r (Analogous to 1/2 × base × height!)
Major Sector: Area of Major Sector = πr² - Area of Minor Sector = [ (360° - θ) / 360° ] × πr²
Quadrant of a Circle: Sector with central angle θ = 90° ⇒ Area = 1/4 πr²
subtopics: Full derivation of arc length and sector area formulas
Connecting clock minute hand rotations to central angles (360° in 60 min ⇒ 6° per min)
Worked Example 1 and Example 2 from NCERT

worked_examples.problem: Example 1 (NCERT): Find the area of the sector of a circle with radius 4 cm and of angle 30°. Also, find the area of the corresponding major sector (Use π = 3.14).
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Radius of circle r = 4 cm
Central angle θ = 30°
Value of π = 3.14.

Step 1: Calculate Area of Minor Sector:
Formula: Area = (θ / 360°) × πr²
Substitute θ = 30°, r = 4:
Area = (30° / 360°) × 3.14 × 4²
= (1 / 12) × 3.14 × 16
= (4 / 3) × 3.14 = 12.56 / 3 ≈ 4.19 cm².

Step 2: Calculate Area of Corresponding Major Sector:
Method 1 (Area subtraction):
Area of Circle = πr² = 3.14 × 4² = 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 cm²
Area of Major Sector = Area of Circle - Area of Minor Sector
= 50.24 - 4.19 = 46.05 cm².

Method 2 (Using major angle 360° - 30° = 330°):
Area = (330° / 360°) × πr² = (11 / 12) × 3.14 × 16 = (44 / 3) × 3.14 = 138.16 / 3 ≈ 46.05 cm².
[ROUGH_WORK]
Both methods match exactly at 46.05 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ Area of minor sector ≈ 4.19 cm², Area of major sector ≈ 46.05 cm² ].

title: Area of Segments: Sector-Triangle Decomposition for 60°, 90° & 120° Angles
description: Master the fundamental geometric decomposition for finding the area of a segment of a circle: Area of Segment = Area of Sector - Area of Triangle OAB. Learn the three standard central angle cases: θ = 60° (Equilateral triangle √3/4 r²), θ = 90° (Right-angled triangle 1/2 r²), and θ = 120° (Isosceles triangle √3/4 r²).
key_concepts: Segment Definition: A circular segment is a region bounded by a chord and the corresponding arc
Fundamental Area Formula: Area of Minor Segment = Area of Sector OAB - Area of Triangle OAB
Major Segment: Area of Major Segment = Area of Circle - Area of Minor Segment
Case 1 (θ = 60°): Since OA = OB = r and ∠AOB = 60°, ΔOAB is equilateral! Area(ΔOAB) = (√3 / 4) r²
Case 2 (θ = 90°): ΔOAB is a right-angled isosceles triangle with legs r and r. Area(ΔOAB) = 1/2 × r × r = 1/2 r²
Case 3 (θ = 120°): Drop perpendicular OM ⊥ AB. OM = r cos 60° = r/2, AB = 2r sin 60° = r√3. Area(ΔOAB) = 1/2 × AB × OM = 1/2 × r√3 × r/2 = (√3 / 4) r²!
subtopics: Geometric proof of triangle area for 60°, 90°, and 120°
Equilateral triangle derivation and altitude properties

worked_examples.problem: Example 3 (NCERT): Find the area of the segment AYB shown in Fig., if radius of the circle is 21 cm and ∠AOB = 120° (Use π = 22/7, √3 = 1.732).
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Radius r = 21 cm
Central angle θ = 120°.
Area of segment AYB = Area of sector OAYB - Area of ΔOAB.

Step 1: Calculate Area of Sector OAYB:
Area of Sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
= (120° / 360°) × (22 / 7) × 21 × 21
= (1 / 3) × 22 × 3 × 21
= 22 × 21 = 462 cm².

Step 2: Calculate Area of ΔOAB:
In ΔOAB, OA = OB = 21 cm, ∠AOB = 120°.
Draw OM ⊥ AB.
Since ΔOAB is isosceles, OM bisects ∠AOB and AB:
∠AOM = ∠BOM = 120° / 2 = 60°.
In right ΔOMA:
OM = OA cos 60° = 21 × (1/2) = 21/2 cm.
AM = OA sin 60° = 21 × (√3/2) = (21√3) / 2 cm.
Chord AB = 2 × AM = 2 × [ (21√3) / 2 ] = 21√3 cm.

Area of ΔOAB = 1/2 × Base × Height
= 1/2 × AB × OM
= 1/2 × (21√3) × (21 / 2)
= (441√3) / 4 cm².

Step 3: Calculate Area of Segment AYB:
Area of Segment = Area of Sector - Area of ΔOAB
= 462 - (441√3 / 4) cm².
If √3 ≈ 1.732:
441 × 1.732 / 4 = 763.812 / 4 = 190.953 cm².
Area of Segment = 462 - 190.953 = 271.047 cm² ≈ 271.05 cm².
[ROUGH_WORK]
Exact CBSE board answer form: [ 462 - (441√3 / 4) ] cm².
Boxed Answer: [ Area of segment = (462 - 441√3 / 4) cm² ≈ 271.05 cm² ].

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 11.1 Q3: The length of the minute hand of a clock is 14 cm. Find the area swept by the minute hand in 5 minutes.
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Length of the minute hand = radius of the circle = r = 14 cm.
Time elapsed = 5 minutes.

Step 1: Calculate central angle θ swept by the minute hand:
In 60 minutes, the minute hand completes 1 full revolution (360°).
Therefore, angle swept in 1 minute = 360° / 60 = 6°.
In 5 minutes, angle swept = θ = 5 × 6° = 30°.

Step 2: Calculate area swept by the minute hand:
The area swept in 5 minutes is a sector of a circle with r = 14 cm and θ = 30°.
Formula: Area = (θ / 360°) × πr²
Substitute θ = 30°, r = 14, π = 22/7:
Area = (30° / 360°) × (22 / 7) × 14 × 14
= (1 / 12) × 22 × 2 × 14
= (1 / 12) × 616
= 616 / 12
Divide numerator and denominator by 4:
= 154 / 3 cm².

In mixed fraction form:
154 / 3 = 51 1/3 cm² ≈ 51.33 cm².
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check: 154 = 3 × 51 + 1.
Boxed Answer: [ Area swept by minute hand = 154/3 cm² (or 51 1/3 cm²) ].

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 11.1 Q4: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends a right angle at the centre. Find the area of the corresponding: (i) minor segment, (ii) major sector. (Use π = 3.14)
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Radius of circle r = 10 cm.
Central angle θ = 90° (right angle).
Value of π = 3.14.

Part (i): Area of Minor Segment
Step 1: Find area of minor sector OAB:
Area of minor sector = (90° / 360°) × πr²
= (1 / 4) × 3.14 × (10)²
= (1 / 4) × 314 = 78.5 cm².

Step 2: Find area of right-angled ΔOAB:
Since ∠AOB = 90°, OA = 10 cm and OB = 10 cm are the perpendicular base and height:
Area(ΔOAB) = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 10 × 10 = 50 cm².

Step 3: Area of Minor Segment:
Area = Area of minor sector - Area(ΔOAB)
= 78.5 - 50 = 28.5 cm².

Part (ii): Area of Major Sector
Central angle for major sector = 360° - 90° = 270°.
Area of major sector = (270° / 360°) × πr²
= (3 / 4) × 3.14 × 100
= 3 × 78.5 = 235.5 cm².
[ROUGH_WORK]
Alternative check for major sector: Area of circle - Area of minor sector = 314 - 78.5 = 235.5 cm² (Verified!).
Boxed Answer: [ (i) Area of minor segment = 28.5 cm², (ii) Area of major sector = 235.5 cm² ].

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 11.1 Q8: A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a square shaped grass field of side 15 m by means of a 5 m long rope. Find: (i) the area of that part of the field in which the horse can graze, (ii) the increase in the grazing area if the rope were 10 m long instead of 5 m. (Use π = 3.14)
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Corner of a square field ⇒ Central angle θ = 90° (Corner of a square is a right angle).
Length of side of square field = 15 m (field is sufficiently large to accommodate the rope).
Value of π = 3.14.

Part (i): Area grazed with 5 m rope (r = 5 m):
The horse can graze in the shape of a quadrant of a circle of radius r1 = 5 m.
Area1 = (90° / 360°) × πr1²
= (1 / 4) × 3.14 × (5)²
= (1 / 4) × 3.14 × 25
= 78.5 / 4 = 19.625 m².

Part (ii): Increase in grazing area if rope is 10 m long (r = 10 m):
With rope length r2 = 10 m, the horse can graze in a quadrant of radius 10 m.
Area2 = (90° / 360°) × πr2²
= (1 / 4) × 3.14 × (10)²
= (1 / 4) × 3.14 × 100
= 314 / 4 = 78.5 m².

Increase in grazing area:
Increase = Area2 - Area1
= 78.5 - 19.625 = 58.875 m².
[ROUGH_WORK]
Notice that doubling the rope from 5 m to 10 m quadruples the total grazing area (2² = 4 times), so the increase is 3 times the original area: 3 × 19.625 = 58.875 m²!
Boxed Answer: [ (i) Grazing area = 19.625 m², (ii) Increase in grazing area = 58.875 m² ].
concept_questions: Why does the horse graze a quadrant instead of a full circle?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 11.1 Q13: A round table cover has six equal designs as shown in Fig. If the radius of the cover is 28 cm, find the cost of making the designs at the rate of ₹ 0.35 per cm². (Use √3 = 1.7)
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Radius of round table cover r = 28 cm.
Number of equal designs = 6.
Rate of making designs = ₹ 0.35 per cm².
Value of √3 = 1.7, π = 22/7.

Step 1: Calculate central angle θ for each design sector:
Since there are 6 equal designs distributed symmetrically around 360°:
θ = 360° / 6 = 60°.
Each design is a minor segment of the circle with r = 28 cm and θ = 60°.

Step 2: Calculate Area of all 6 Sectors:
Total Area of 6 sectors = 6 × [ (60° / 360°) × πr² ]
= 6 × (1 / 6) × (22 / 7) × 28 × 28
= 1 × (22 / 7) × 784
= 22 × 112 = 2464 cm².

Step 3: Calculate Area of all 6 Triangles:
Since θ = 60° and OA = OB = 28 cm, each triangle is equilateral.
Area of 1 equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) r² = (√3 / 4) × 28² = (√3 / 4) × 784 = 196√3 cm².
Total Area of 6 triangles = 6 × 196√3 = 1176√3 cm².
Substitute √3 = 1.7:
Total Area of 6 triangles = 1176 × 1.7 = 1999.2 cm².

Step 4: Calculate Total Area of the 6 Designs:
Total Area of Designs = (Total Area of 6 Sectors) - (Total Area of 6 Triangles)
= 2464 - 1999.2 = 464.8 cm².

Step 5: Calculate Total Cost:
Total Cost = Total Area × Rate per cm²
= 464.8 × ₹ 0.35
= ₹ 162.68.
[ROUGH_WORK]
464.8 × 0.35 = 464.8 × (7 / 20) = 23.24 × 7 = 162.68.
Boxed Answer: [ Total cost of making designs = ₹ 162.68 ].
